\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{പിണക്കം} (piṇakkaṁ)}{പിണക്കം (piṇakkaṁ)}]{\ml{പിണക്കം} (piṇakkaṁ) — a falling-out; a sulk}

\label{lesson:ML-C556-pinakkam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to split up, then the Malayalam for to be reconciled.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{പിണക്കം}}
\textbf{\ml{പിണക്കം}} — \emph{piṇakkaṁ} — \textquotedblleft{}a falling-out; a sulk\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ചെറിയ} \ml{പിണക്കം} \ml{കാരണം} \ml{അവർ} \ml{രണ്ട്} \ml{ദിവസം} \ml{സംസാരിച്ചില്ല}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ceṟiya piṇakkaṁ kāraṇaṁ avar raṇṭŭ divasaṁ saṁsāriccilla.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Because of a small falling-out they did not talk for two days.
\end{quote}

The noun of \ml{പിണങ്ങുക}, to sulk, already familiar.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{പിണക്കം}} (\emph{piṇakkaṁ}) is native Dravidian, the noun of \ml{പിണങ്ങുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to fall out\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 4160).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{piṇakkaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{piṇakkaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ceṟiya piṇakkaṁ kāraṇaṁ avar raṇṭŭ divasaṁ saṁsāriccilla.} — Because of a small falling-out they did not talk for two days.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to split up, then the Malayalam for to be reconciled, then say \emph{piṇakkaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{പിണക്കം} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A falling-out; a sulk\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ചതിക്കുക} (catikkuka)}{ചതിക്കുക (catikkuka)}]{\ml{ചതിക്കുക} (catikkuka) — to betray; to cheat}

\label{lesson:ML-C556-catikkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to be reconciled, then the Malayalam for a falling-out.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ചതിക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{ചതിക്കുക}} — \emph{catikkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to betray; to cheat\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{വിശ്വസിച്ച} \ml{സുഹൃത്ത്} \ml{അവനെ} \ml{ചതിച്ചു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{viśvasicca suhṛttŭ avane caticcu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The friend he trusted cheated him.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{ചതിച്ചു}, \emph{caticcu}.

The noun is \ml{ചതി}, a trick; one who cheats is \ml{ചതിയൻ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ചതിക്കുക}} (\emph{catikkuka}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 2323 lists \ml{ചതി}, \textquotedblleft{}deceit, treachery\textquotedblright{}, and the verb, to cheat and betray (DEDR 2323).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{catikkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{catikkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{viśvasicca suhṛttŭ avane caticcu.} — The friend he trusted cheated him.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to be reconciled, then the Malayalam for a falling-out, then say \emph{catikkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ചതിക്കുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To betray; to cheat\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{വഞ്ചന} (vañcana)}{വഞ്ചന (vañcana)}]{\ml{വഞ്ചന} (vañcana) — betrayal; deceit}

\label{lesson:ML-C556-vancana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a falling-out, then the Malayalam for to betray.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{വഞ്ചന}}
\textbf{\ml{വഞ്ചന}} — \emph{vañcana} — \textquotedblleft{}betrayal; deceit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{പണം} \ml{എടുത്ത്} \ml{ഓടിപ്പോയത്} \ml{വലിയ} \ml{വഞ്ചനയായിരുന്നു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{paṇaṁ eṭuttŭ ōṭippōyatŭ valiya vañcanayāyirunnu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Running off with the money was a great betrayal.
\end{quote}

Formal; \ml{വഞ്ചിക്കുക} is to deceive.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{വഞ്ചന}} (\emph{vañcana}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{vañcana}, \textquotedblleft{}cheating, deception, fraud\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vañcana}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vañcana}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paṇaṁ eṭuttŭ ōṭippōyatŭ valiya vañcanayāyirunnu.} — Running off with the money was a great betrayal.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a falling-out, then the Malayalam for to betray, then say \emph{vañcana} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{വഞ്ചന} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Betrayal; deceit\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{കരുതൽ} (karutal)}{കരുതൽ (karutal)}]{\ml{കരുതൽ} (karutal) — care; concern}

\label{lesson:ML-C556-karutal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to betray, then the Malayalam for betrayal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{കരുതൽ}}
\textbf{\ml{കരുതൽ}} — \emph{karutal} — \textquotedblleft{}care; concern\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{രോഗിയായ} \ml{അച്ഛനോട്} \ml{മകൾ} \ml{വലിയ} \ml{കരുതൽ} \ml{കാണിച്ചു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rōgiyāya acchanōṭŭ makaḷ valiya karutal kāṇiccu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The daughter showed great care for her sick father.
\end{quote}

From \ml{കരുതുക}, to keep in mind; \ml{കരുതലോടെ} means carefully.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{കരുതൽ}} (\emph{karutal}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 1283 gives it as care and regard, beside \ml{കരുതുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to think, to attend to\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 1283).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{karutal}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{karutal}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rōgiyāya acchanōṭŭ makaḷ valiya karutal kāṇiccu.} — The daughter showed great care for her sick father.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to betray, then the Malayalam for betrayal, then say \emph{karutal} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{കരുതൽ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Care; concern\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{പരിഗണന} (parigaṇana)}{പരിഗണന (parigaṇana)}]{\ml{പരിഗണന} (parigaṇana) — consideration}

\label{lesson:ML-C556-pariganana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for betrayal, then the Malayalam for care.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{പരിഗണന}}
\textbf{\ml{പരിഗണന}} — \emph{parigaṇana} — \textquotedblleft{}consideration\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{പ്രായമായവർക്ക്} \ml{ബസിൽ} \ml{പ്രത്യേക} \ml{പരിഗണന} \ml{കിട്ടണം}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{prāyamāyavarkkŭ basil pratyēka parigaṇana kiṭṭaṇaṁ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Elderly people should get special consideration on the bus.
\end{quote}

\ml{പരിഗണിക്കുക} is to consider.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{പരിഗണന}} (\emph{parigaṇana}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{parigaṇana}, a reckoning or counting over (Monier-Williams): to consider someone is to count them in.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{parigaṇana}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{parigaṇana}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prāyamāyavarkkŭ basil pratyēka parigaṇana kiṭṭaṇaṁ.} — Elderly people should get special consideration on the bus.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for betrayal, then the Malayalam for care, then say \emph{parigaṇana} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{പരിഗണന} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Consideration\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 549–556 — a review}

\label{lesson:ML-R556-review-549-556}



\begin{quote}
Say the Malayalam for proficiency and a fee.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item proficiency, a fee, a career, a pay rise, to bear a load
  \item a workplace, supervision, to coordinate, to consult, an interval
  \item to entrust, to take on, to attain, to put in work, to toil
  \item a relationship, married life, a love letter, a boyfriend, to be in love
  \item a cradle, to adopt, a stepmother, a sibling, a brother
  \item a sister, parents, a brother-in-law, a sister-in-law, a family member
  \item a lullaby, a joint family, a nuclear family, to split up, to be reconciled
  \item a falling-out, to betray, betrayal, care, consideration
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Proficiency? (\textbf{\ml{നൈപുണ്യം}}, \emph{naipuṇyaṁ}.) A fee? (\textbf{\ml{പ്രതിഫലം}}, \emph{pratiphalaṁ}.) A career? (\textbf{\ml{കരിയർ}}, \emph{kariyar}.) A pay rise? (\textbf{\ml{ശമ്പളവർദ്ധന}}, \emph{śampaḷavarddhana}.) To bear a load? (\textbf{\ml{വഹിക്കുക}}, \emph{vahikkuka}.) A workplace? (\textbf{\ml{ജോലിസ്ഥലം}}, \emph{jōlisthalaṁ}.) Supervision? (\textbf{\ml{മേൽനോട്ടം}}, \emph{mēlnōṭṭaṁ}.) To coordinate? (\textbf{\ml{ഏകോപിപ്പിക്കുക}}, \emph{ēkōpippikkuka}.) To consult? (\textbf{\ml{കൂടിയാലോചിക്കുക}}, \emph{kūṭiyālōcikkuka}.) An interval? (\textbf{\ml{ഇടവേള}}, \emph{iṭavēḷa}.) To entrust? (\textbf{\ml{ഏൽപ്പിക്കുക}}, \emph{ēlppikkuka}.) To take on? (\textbf{\ml{ഏറ്റെടുക്കുക}}, \emph{ēṟṟeṭukkuka}.) To attain? (\textbf{\ml{കൈവരിക്കുക}}, \emph{kaivarikkuka}.) To put in work? (\textbf{\ml{പണിയെടുക്കുക}}, \emph{paṇiyeṭukkuka}.) To toil? (\textbf{\ml{അധ്വാനിക്കുക}}, \emph{adhvānikkuka}.) A relationship? (\textbf{\ml{ബന്ധം}}, \emph{bandhaṁ}.) Married life? (\textbf{\ml{ദാമ്പത്യം}}, \emph{dāmpatyaṁ}.) A love letter? (\textbf{\ml{പ്രണയലേഖനം}}, \emph{praṇayalēkhanaṁ}.) A boyfriend? (\textbf{\ml{കാമുകൻ}}, \emph{kāmukan}.) To be in love? (\textbf{\ml{പ്രണയിക്കുക}}, \emph{praṇayikkuka}.) A cradle? (\textbf{\ml{തൊട്ടിൽ}}, \emph{toṭṭil}.) To adopt? (\textbf{\ml{ദത്തെടുക്കുക}}, \emph{datteṭukkuka}.) A stepmother? (\textbf{\ml{രണ്ടാനമ്മ}}, \emph{raṇṭānamma}.) A sibling? (\textbf{\ml{കൂടപ്പിറപ്പ്}}, \emph{kūṭappiṟappŭ}.) A brother? (\textbf{\ml{സഹോദരൻ}}, \emph{sahōdaran}.) A sister? (\textbf{\ml{സഹോദരി}}, \emph{sahōdari}.) Parents? (\textbf{\ml{മാതാപിതാക്കൾ}}, \emph{mātāpitākkaḷ}.) A brother-in-law? (\textbf{\ml{അളിയൻ}}, \emph{aḷiyan}.) A sister-in-law? (\textbf{\ml{നാത്തൂൻ}}, \emph{nāttūn}.) A family member? (\textbf{\ml{കുടുംബാംഗം}}, \emph{kuṭumbāṁgaṁ}.) A lullaby? (\textbf{\ml{താരാട്ട്}}, \emph{tārāṭṭŭ}.) A joint family? (\textbf{\ml{കൂട്ടുകുടുംബം}}, \emph{kūṭṭukuṭumbaṁ}.) A nuclear family? (\textbf{\ml{അണുകുടുംബം}}, \emph{aṇukuṭumbaṁ}.) To split up? (\textbf{\ml{വേർപിരിയുക}}, \emph{vērpiriyuka}.) To be reconciled? (\textbf{\ml{ഇണങ്ങുക}}, \emph{iṇaṅṅuka}.) A falling-out? (\textbf{\ml{പിണക്കം}}, \emph{piṇakkaṁ}.) To betray? (\textbf{\ml{ചതിക്കുക}}, \emph{catikkuka}.) Betrayal? (\textbf{\ml{വഞ്ചന}}, \emph{vañcana}.) Care? (\textbf{\ml{കരുതൽ}}, \emph{karutal}.) Consideration? (\textbf{\ml{പരിഗണന}}, \emph{parigaṇana}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
